method: Free-space delta on the measured volume, sampled with `df -k /` immediately before and after the operation with a `sync` on each side. Free-space delta is the only way to observe copy-on-write sharing on APFS, because st_blocks reports every clone at full size.
caveat: The host is a shared workstation, so free-space delta carries background noise. It is used only where the signal dwarfs that noise (two orders of magnitude), and never as the source for a headline byte total.

experiments.operation: git clone --no-hardlinks <local object source> && git checkout --detach <revision>
experiments.interpretation: A fresh clone genuinely consumes its reported size. Git writes new object files rather than cloning blocks, so copy-on-write does not reduce the cost of an additional full checkout.

experiments.operation: tools/install_worker_dependencies.sh --offline against an already-populated shared store
experiments.interpretation: The dependency view costs about 2 MiB of real disk despite reporting roughly 317 MiB. pnpm imports packages with clone-or-copy, which resolves to an APFS clonefile, so the view shares blocks with the shared store. On this filesystem class the second and later dependency views are effectively free, and node_modules is not a meaningful footprint-reduction target.

portability_warning: This result is filesystem-class specific. On a filesystem without reflink support (for example ext4 on the hosted CI runners) pnpm falls back to hard links, which also share blocks, but on a filesystem with neither reflink nor hard-link support the same install would copy the full payload. Do not generalise the 2 MiB figure beyond copy-on-write or hard-link capable filesystems.
